Case Study 1: Malaria & Micro-Hydrology - Peruvian Amazon

Source: vignettes/case1_peru_amazon_malaria.Rmd
case1_peru_amazon_malaria.Rmd

1. Epidemiological Context & Landscape Ecology

In the Peruvian Amazon (e.g., Loreto, Ucayali, Madre de Dios), Anopheles darlingi is the primary vector driving endemic malaria transmission (Plasmodium vivax and P. falciparum).

Unlike macro-scale satellite products (MODIS, Landsat) that fail to detect puddles obscured under dense primary or secondary canopy, ultra-high resolution drone orthomosaics capture: 1. Micro-topographic drainage sinks and slow-moving stream margins. 2. Artificial water depressions created by illegal gold mining pits (minería aluvial) and fish farming ponds (piscigranjas). 3. Peridomestic vector flight buffers (100−250 m100 - 250\text{ m}) from riverine indigenous and rural settlements.

2. Targeted Indicator Suite

Indicator Implementation Entomological Significance
NDVI / NDRE d4h_ndvi(), d4h_ndre() Quantifies dense canopy shading that shelters adult Anopheles during hot diurnal hours.
NDWI / IRHE d4h_ndwi(), d4h_irhe() Detects open water surfaces and turbid, stagnant water bodies in deforested clearings.
Slope & TWI d4h_slope(), d4h_twi() Identifies flat terrain (β<3∘\beta < 3^\circ) with high wetness accumulation prone to persistent flooding.
Buffer Focal Analysis d4h_indicator_buffer() Limits statistical computation to the biologically relevant vector foraging radius around households.
Euclidean Risk Decay d4h_distance_to_risk() Computes risk of transmission as an exponential decay function Ri=∑e−dij/λR_i = \sum e^{-d_{ij}/\lambda}.

3. End-to-End Execution Workflow 

library(drones4health)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

# File paths to UAV orthomosaics
img_dir  <- "data/peru_amazon"
path_rgb <- file.path(img_dir, "Ohuay_D.tif")    # Orthomosaic
path_nir <- file.path(img_dir, "Ohuay_NIR.tif")  # Near Infrared
path_r   <- file.path(img_dir, "Ohuay_R.tif")    # Red
path_re  <- file.path(img_dir, "Ohuay_RE.tif")   # Red Edge
xlsx_houses <- "nuevas_casas_localizadas.xlsx"

# Step 1: Focal NDVI Buffer around native riverine houses (150m buffer)
res_buffer <- d4h_indicator_buffer(
  indicator   = "NDVI",
  houses      = xlsx_houses,
  radius      = 3,            # 3 grid cells
  cell_size   = 50,           # 50m cell size = 150m buffer
  nir         = path_nir,
  red         = path_r,
  palette     = "viridis",
  title       = "Malaria Vector Flight Range (150m): Focal NDVI & River Margins"
)

# Step 2: Surface Water Segmentation
r_ndvi <- d4h_ndvi(nir = path_nir, red = path_r)

water_bodies <- d4h_segment_water(
  raster_in            = r_ndvi,
  rgb_raster           = path_rgb,
  max_water_brightness = 90.0,   # Avoid bright metal roofs misclassification
  threshold            = -0.15,
  min_area_m2          = 15.0    # Detect small larvae habitats
)

# Step 3: Proximity Risk from Household to Larval Habitats
casas_riesgo <- d4h_distance_to_risk(
  buildings    = res_buffer$houses,
  sources      = water_bodies,
  decay_lambda = 100.0          # 100m mean dispersal parameter
)

# Summary of exposure
table(casas_riesgo$risk_level)
# Critico (<50m): 30 casas | Alto (50-100m): 16 casas | Moderado: 3 casas | Bajo: 6 casas

# Step 4: Executive Zonal Grid Summary
d4h_export_summary(
  raster_in   = res_buffer$raster,
  output_file = "Reporte_Malaria_Loreto_Perú.xlsx",
  cell_size   = 100
)

4. Operational Health Decision Support

  • Targeted Larviciding: Direct field teams with Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (BTI) exclusively to water polygons classified within the Critical category (<50 m<50\text{ m}).
  • Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS): Prioritize houses located within 100 m100\text{ m} of flood sinks during the onset of the seasonal river recession.
